questions.q: Why add a Territory slicer even though the report is scoped to one stakeholder's region?
options: The query returns every territory, so a slicer lets the manager narrow to their own region or compare against others without rebuilding the report
Power BI requires at least one slicer on every published report
Slicers are necessary for KPI cards to display any value at all
A slicer is the only way to add a Territory column to the data model
questions.explain: Lesson 1 kept all territories in the data for context, and a slicer gives the Southeast manager one-click control over which territories the page shows.

questions.q: Why do the KPI cards, bar chart, and table all recalculate automatically when the Territory slicer selection changes?
options: Because Total Sales, Order Count, and Average Order Value are DAX measures, which respond dynamically to whatever filters are applied
Because the slicer directly edits the underlying T-SQL query every time it's used
Because Power Query reruns automatically whenever a slicer is touched
Because the report was published to the Power BI Service
questions.explain: This is the exact payoff described in Lesson 6: measures recalculate under any filter context, so no extra wiring is needed when a slicer is added.

questions.q: What number format does the lesson recommend for the Order Count measure?
options: A whole number with a thousands separator and no currency symbol
Currency format with two decimal places
Percentage format
Currency format with no decimal places
questions.explain: Order Count isn't a dollar amount, so it gets a plain whole-number format with a thousands separator, unlike Total Sales or Average Order Value.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend setting number formats on the measure itself rather than per-visual?
options: Formatting the measure once means every card, chart, and table using it automatically inherits the same format
Power BI does not allow number formatting to be set on individual visuals
Per-visual formatting is only available in the Power BI Service, not Desktop
Measure-level formatting is required before a measure can be used in a slicer
questions.explain: Setting the format once on the measure (via Measure tools > Formatting) avoids re-formatting the same number separately on every visual that uses it.

questions.q: What's wrong with a default visual title like 'Sum of TotalSalesAmount by Territory'?
options: It describes what field is on the chart rather than stating the answer to the stakeholder's actual question
It exceeds Power BI's character limit for visual titles
It cannot be changed once the visual is created
It references a column that no longer exists after the measures were created
questions.explain: A title like 'Sales by Region' reads as an answer; the default title just repeats field names, which matters most for a quick, single-glance report.
